speaker: Doctor
text: What were you doing exactly when the vertigo first started? Did you notice any ringing in your ears or hearing loss at the same time?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since the episode was brief (3 minutes) and has now resolved, was there a specific head movement or position change, such as turning in bed, that triggered it? Also, did you experience any new weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking during that time?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). Given the brief duration of the episode and the absence of neurological deficits like weakness or speech difficulties, BPPV is the most likely diagnosis. I recommend performing the Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm this.
